short: CASZ1 is the single human orthologue of Drosophila castor, a large multi-zinc-finger transcription factor that in flies specifies a late temporal window of neuroblast identity. The human gene sits at 1p36.22 and produces two main isoforms with different numbers of C2H2 zinc fingers. Its binding preference is poorly characterized: the only motif in these databases is a long, AT-rich composite model from in vitro selection, and no consensus has been established by focused biochemistry. CASZ1 is required for cardiac and vascular morphogenesis in Xenopus and mouse, its expression is low in high-risk neuroblastoma where 1p36 is frequently deleted, and common variants at the CASZ1 locus are among the earliest replicated blood-pressure associations.
long:
## The factors

CASZ1 (castor zinc finger 1, CST, ZNF693) is the vertebrate orthologue of Drosophila castor, which was
cloned in 1992 as a novel zinc-finger protein required for the development of a subset of CNS neurons and
is best known as one of the temporal identity factors that mark a late window in neuroblast lineages. The
human gene is at 1p36.22. It encodes a large protein with multiple C2H2 zinc fingers arranged in an
unusual pattern, and two principal isoforms are described, commonly referred to by their finger counts
(an eleven-finger and a five-finger form), which differ at the C terminus. CASZ1 binds DNA as a monomer
as far as is known; no obligate dimerization partner has been reported, though it associates with
congenital heart disease protein 5 (CHD5/CONGDD) and with chromatin-remodelling activity in cardiac
tissue. There is one human gene, so there is no paralogue problem within the family, but there is also
very little comparative information to lean on. Expression is highest in heart, vasculature and
neural-crest-derived sympathetic tissue, with additional expression in kidney and lung.

## The motif

This family has no established consensus, and this entry does not invent one. The only model in these
databases is a single HOCOMOCO matrix, CASZ1.H14CORE.0.SGI.A, with the data consensus
TTTTGGGGNAAAATNNGNNDTTT - a 23-position, mostly AT-rich composite with two loosely specified blocks
separated by a degenerate middle. Its evidence code (S, G, I) includes in vitro selection and integrative
data and it carries a grade-A quality flag, so the measurement is credible as a measurement; what is
missing is independent confirmation and any focused structural or mutational work assigning positions to
particular fingers. There is no JASPAR, CIS-BP or Vierstra model for CASZ1 in this atlas, so cohesion is
undefined (recorded as zero because there is nothing to compare against), and the motif's nearest
neighbour in any other family reaches only about 0.64 similarity - it does not clearly resemble any other
known element.

A long AT-rich model with a degenerate middle behaves in a scan much like a low-complexity filter. The
information is spread thinly over many positions, poly-T and poly-A tracts will score, and the effective
specificity is much lower than the length of the model suggests. Nothing is known about half-sites,
spacing rules or which of the many CASZ1 zinc fingers contact DNA. Whether the two isoforms have different
specificities has not been tested.

## Where it acts

Direct, validated CASZ1 target genes are few. The best-characterized is EGFL7, which CASZ1 binds and
activates in endothelial cells; CASZ1 depletion phenocopies EGFL7 loss in vascular sprouting, and
restoring Egfl7 rescues the defect, acting through RhoA and focal-adhesion localization. In neuroblastoma
cells, restoring CASZ1 changes the expression of a broad set of growth- and differentiation-related genes,
but these were identified by expression profiling rather than by direct occupancy, so most are downstream
rather than bound. Genome-wide occupancy maps for CASZ1 in human cells are sparse. The practical
consequence is that there is no established picture of whether CASZ1 works from promoters or enhancers,
what chromatin context its sites occupy, or which factors it co-occurs with. The literature here is thin
and should be described as thin.

## Biology and disease

CASZ1 is required for heart and blood-vessel development. In Xenopus, loss of CASZ1 blocks differentiation
of cardiac precursor cells at the ventral midline, and CASZ1-depleted embryos fail to form a branched,
lumenized vascular network; human endothelial cells depleted of CASZ1 show altered adhesion, morphology
and sprouting. CASZ1 associates with CHD5 to maintain myocardial tissue integrity. In humans, a
heterozygous CASZ1 missense variant (p.L38P) segregating with ventricular septal defect in one family was
reported with reduced transactivation in reporter assays, the first link between CASZ1 and congenital
heart disease; this rests on a single pedigree and should be treated as suggestive. In neuroblastoma, low
CASZ1 expression correlates with older age at diagnosis, high-risk classification, 1p loss of
heterozygosity and MYCN amplification, and with worse survival; restoring CASZ1 in neuroblastoma lines
induces differentiation and suppresses tumorigenicity, making it a candidate for the 1p36 tumour
suppressor. Separately, common variants at the CASZ1 locus were among the loci identified in early
genome-wide association studies of blood pressure and hypertension, though the causal gene and mechanism
at that locus have not been settled.

## Reading a hit

Treat a CASZ1 match as weak. The model is a single long AT-rich composite from one database; there is no
replication across databases, no structure, and no defined core, so a match does not license the
conclusion that CASZ1 bound the sequence. AT-rich models of this shape also overlap the preferences of
homeodomain, forkhead, HMG and other minor-groove AT readers, and they score poly-A/poly-T tracts, so
sequence composition alone can produce hits. There is no paralogue ambiguity within the family, because
there is only one gene, but that is not reassurance - it just means the usual family-versus-member caveat
is replaced by a cruder one: the motif itself is not well enough established to support a specific call.
Use a CASZ1 hit as a hypothesis to test with expression and occupancy data in a tissue where CASZ1 is
actually expressed (heart, endothelium, sympathetic neuroblast lineage), and do not build an argument on
the match alone.
caveats: The whole family rests on one HOCOMOCO matrix, a 23-position AT-rich composite with a degenerate middle. Its evidence includes in vitro selection at grade A, so the measurement is credible, but there is no independent model in JASPAR, CIS-BP or Vierstra to corroborate it, cohesion is undefined, and no structural or mutational work assigns positions to specific zinc fingers. Long AT-rich models function partly as low-complexity filters: poly-A and poly-T tracts score, and the preferences overlap homeodomain, forkhead and HMG factors. Whether the two CASZ1 isoforms differ in specificity is untested. There is only one human gene, so no paralogue problem - but a match should be treated as a hypothesis, not an identification.
